newsitem.title: USA: CBOT SOYMEAL AND SOYOIL END LOWER AS SOYBEANS FALL.
newsitem.headline: CBOT SOYMEAL AND SOYOIL END LOWER AS SOYBEANS FALL.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended down half the daily limit on Thursday, in line with sharp losses in soybeans linked to outlooks for rain this weekend in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
Crop forecasts that suggested a record soybean crop in the fields also contributed to the declines, they said.
Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio said weekend storms would likely bring 0.25 to 0.75 inch of rain to the U.S. Midwest with 40 to 50 percent coverage.
But there was a chance that a second system brewing in the southern U.S. would bring heavier precipitation, he said.

Farmers Commodities Corp's U.S. soybean crop production estimate, released on Wednesday, was also bearish, sources said. FCC put soybean output at 2.73 billion bushels. That figure was above USDA's July outlook for 2.69 billion bushels.

If realized, a 2.73-billion-bushel soybean crop would be record large. It was also the highest estimate in a Reuter survey of analysts released on Thursday. That survey produced an average crop production estimate of 2.68 billion bushels.
Soymeal ended $6.30 to $4.70 per ton lower with December down $5.60 at $208.80 a ton. Soyoil closed 0.55 to 0.27 cent per lb lower with December down 0.53 at 22.22 cents.
On the day, Produce Grain was a key buyer of 500 lots December soyoil and 300 lots September. Cargill Inc and ADM were light slellers while Refco Inc sold 300 December.
In soyoil, Refco sold 300 December while Merrill Lynch and Smith Barney each sold 200 December.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 15,000 lots, against Wednesday's actual volume of 14,017 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 13,000 lots, against Wednesday's 14,667.
